planned_outcome: Land HMS Ambush research mission: empirically test whether Method 3 (1D heat-equation inverse problem) can extrapolate x_core past the probe tip on the existing real CSVs, characterise its parameter confidence (Hessian + bootstrap), and quantify robustness under sigma=0.5/1.0/2.0 deg C noise. Output is a research report with a clear go/no-go recommendation; no production wiring.
actual_outcome: Verdict NO-GO for Method 3 production wiring. Synthetic recovery passes (bias 0.0006, spread 0.003, 93 percent coverage). Real-CSV RMSE 6-10 C exceeds the 2 C bar; alpha-x_core correlation 0.9 on convergent cases (degenerate inverse problem); 2/7 lidded cases pathological with non-physical alpha; no BA3C case extrapolates past T1. Report at tests/baselines/heat_equation_extrapolation_research.md with recommendation to use Method 1 (relaxed parabolic clamp) or Method 4 (loaf-thickness metadata) instead.
success_metric_result: Synthetic recovery passes; real-CSV evidence supports NO-GO; phase 3 robustness sweep stopped before completion (per-fit speed on real data was 27x slower than synthetic, would have taken 4+ hours).

adopt: Always report parameter correlation rho alongside CIs for 2-parameter inverse problems — marginal CIs are misleading when |rho| > 0.8
avoid: Sizing slow-path runtime budgets on synthetic data only; real-CSV time-grids can be much longer and the per-fit cost can scale 27x
